note:
Declared cross-file leakage, recorded at the HIGHEST value seen across environments. The ratchet forbids only growth, so a machine that leaks less still passes — and CI, lacking some packages this container has, stubs more of them and leaks more. A baseline recorded only locally fails CI forever on a difference that is not a defect. `replaced` stays at zero everywhere: see scripts/security/check_test_isolation.py.

2026-08-05: rose from 7 files / 11 env / 26 added to 19 / 36 / 35. Leakage did not grow — the detector's scope did. It hooked only pytest_runtest_protocol, which fires after collection has already imported every test module, so every module-scope os.environ[...] and sys.modules[...] write in the repository sat inside the plugin's own baseline and was structurally invisible. It now brackets each module's import as well. The gap cost a full-suite collection abort (test_checkpoint.py set REDIS_URL to the empty string; dashboard/app.py rightly refuses to import on that) which this plugin watched happen and could not see. The same widening also surfaced two real module-identity collisions on the generic names `app` and `introspect_app`, both now scoped.
